purpose: One approved exact preinstalled Android SDK removal on one fresh disposable GitHub Ubuntu VM, followed by a capacity check and, only with sufficient capacity, one frozen setup probe. Not native qualification.
approval_context: After receiving the detailed exact-target cleanup, bounded one-shot workflow, non-recoverability and stop-on-insufficient-space explanation, the user asked to resume this work.

cleanup.host_premise: Trusted fresh disposable GitHub-hosted VM without concurrent writers; exclusion of concurrent writers is a premise, not a verified report claim.
cleanup.ownership_policy: Bind and recheck observed device, inode, mode, UID and GID; do not assume all provider SDK entries are root-owned.
cleanup.descendant_symlink_policy: Unlink the leaf without opening or following its target.
cleanup.mount_policy: Reject target and descendant mountpoints from bounded Linux mountinfo plus cross-device nodes; SDK and /tmp must share device.
cleanup.recovery: No rollback after started deletion; reinstall or replace the disposable VM. Never retry this attempt.
cleanup.insufficient_capacity_action: Stop after reporting capacity; do not call setup probe or delete additional targets.

execution.required_runtime: CPython 3.12 Linux x86_64 root, isolated no-site no-bytecode
execution.local_validation: Owned synthetic temporary directories only; no local real SDK deletion or native setup invocation.

capacity.requirement: max(fragment-rounded ZIP plus TAR, unchanged 16 GiB floor plus fragment-rounded TAR)
capacity.subsequent_job: Fresh image; must carry separately reviewed same-target preparation into any future approved qualification.

result_semantics.observed_means: Exact SDK removal and capacity measurement completed; may still report insufficient capacity.
result_semantics.readiness_means: Current setup and theoretical headroom checks only; neither full qualification nor new execution authorization.
result_semantics.missing_or_failed_report: No success claim and no retry; retain any partial-deletion state that is verifiable.
